correctness.rationale: The claim is sign(D_n) for D_n=Δ²(log M_n(q)/n). Möbius inversion and a geometric correction bound give the uniform analytic estimates. Exact rational comparisons start ratio inductions at n=6 for q>=9 and n=23 for all q>=2. Closed small-index formulas establish D_3>0, D_4<0 and D_5<0 for q>=6. Exact integer powers certify 115 remaining strict inequalities and 7 sharp counter-witnesses; 168 independent Möbius-inversion identities cross-check. No finite census is substituted for an infinite argument.

originality.rationale: The 2012 originating paper gives the exact threshold values as a conjectural remark only and its theorem covers n>=5.835×10^14. A 2026 source proves different normalized and unrooted statements. Seven relevant semantic published-finding corpus searches and direct literature searches found no proof of the sharp rooted cutoffs; priority remains conditional on the documented residual risks.
residual_risks: Historical mathematical priority remains provisional: an exact sharp cutoff proof could exist in unindexed or differently titled literature.
Originality of finite-field cutoffs themselves is not asserted: they are explicitly proposed in Sun 2012; novelty is the complete proof and integer-alphabet extension.
The embedded finite certificate is transparent but has not undergone independent mathematical audit or external replay.

value.rationale: This fully proves the exact sharp numerical cutoff conjecture stated in 2012 for irreducible-polynomial counts, with strict reverse witnesses at every boundary, and extends to all finite alphabets. The universal bounds and finite certificate explain the exceptional thresholds rather than merely reciting an observed table. The natural integer sequence and exact roots-ratio invariant are independently motivated by primitive necklaces and irreducibles.
